tasks.title: Set up Room database and core data model
tasks.description: Create the Room database with all core entity tables (device_item, cloud_item, media_group, match, transfer_job, origin_rule, picker_round) and DAOs for data access. This is the foundation for all data persistence in the app.
tasks.details:
1. Add Room dependencies to gradle/libs.versions.toml (androidx.room:room-runtime, room-ktx, room-compiler via KSP).
2. Add KSP plugin to build.gradle.kts for Room annotation processing.
3. Create package `com.gankdat.pomegranate.data.db`.
4. Define entities:
   - `DeviceItemEntity`: id (Long PK), volume (String), relativePath, bucket, displayName, mime, size (Long), dateTaken (Long), dateModified (Long), width (Int), height (Int), durationMs (Long?), fingerprint (String), sha256 (String?).
   - `CloudItemEntity`: id (Long PK), pickerMediaItemId (String unique), sessionId (String), filename, mime, type, createTime (Long), width, height, durationMs, cameraMake?, cameraModel?, baseUrl, baseUrlExpiresAt (Long), inferredOrigin?, userOverrideOrigin?.
   - `MediaGroupEntity`: id (Long PK), kind (enum: SINGLE, LIVE_PHOTO, MOTION_PHOTO, RAW_PAIR, EDIT_PAIR).
   - `DeviceItemGroupCrossRef` and `CloudItemGroupCrossRef` for many-to-many.
   - `MatchEntity`: cloudItemId (FK), deviceItemId (FK), confidence (enum: EXACT, LIKELY, AMBIGUOUS), evidence (String JSON).
   - `TransferJobEntity`: id (Long PK), cloudItemId (FK), state (enum: QUEUED, RUNNING, VERIFYING, DONE, FAILED, PAUSED), destinationUri, bytesExpected, bytesWritten, sha256?, fidelity (enum: ORIGINAL, GPS_STRIPPED, TRANSCODED), attempts, lastError?.
   - `OriginRuleEntity`: id (Long PK), source (enum: LEARNED, BUILTIN), pattern, originLabel, confidence (Float).
   - `PickerRoundEntity`: sessionId (String PK), createdAt (Long), itemCount (Int), state (String).
5. Create type converters for enums.
6. Create DAOs with basic CRUD + query methods.
7. Create `PomegranateDatabase` abstract class annotated with @Database.
8. Write unit tests for entity creation and basic DAO operations.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit tests using Room's in-memory database: test insert/query/update/delete for each entity; test type converters; test foreign key constraints; test cross-reference queries for media groups.

subtasks.title: Create DeviceItemEntity and CloudItemEntity with Room annotations
subtasks.description: Define the two primary media item entities representing device-local files and cloud-fetched items with all required fields and proper Room annotations.
subtasks.details:
1. Create package com.gankdat.pomegranate.data.db.entity
2. Create DeviceItemEntity.kt:
   @Entity(tableName = "device_item", indices = [Index("fingerprint")])
   - id: Long (PrimaryKey, autoGenerate)
   - volume: String, relativePath: String, bucket: String, displayName: String
   - mime: String, size: Long, dateTaken: Long, dateModified: Long
   - width: Int, height: Int, durationMs: Long? (nullable for photos)
   - fingerprint: String (computed hash of filename+size+dateTaken+dimensions)
   - sha256: String? (nullable, computed on demand)
3. Create CloudItemEntity.kt:
   @Entity(tableName = "cloud_item", indices = [Index("pickerMediaItemId", unique = true), Index("sessionId")])
   - id: Long (PrimaryKey, autoGenerate)
   - pickerMediaItemId: String (unique), sessionId: String
   - filename: String, mime: String, type: String
   - createTime: Long, width: Int, height: Int, durationMs: Long?
   - cameraMake: String?, cameraModel: String?
   - baseUrl: String, baseUrlExpiresAt: Long
   - inferredOrigin: String?, userOverrideOrigin: String?
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit test entity creation with Room's in-memory database. Verify insert and query operations work correctly. Test unique constraint on pickerMediaItemId rejects duplicates.

subtasks.title: Create MatchEntity and TransferJobEntity with enum fields
subtasks.description: Define the MatchEntity for cloud-to-device reconciliation results and TransferJobEntity for tracking download jobs with their various states and fidelity levels.
subtasks.details:
1. Create enums in com.gankdat.pomegranate.data.db.entity:
   - MatchConfidence: EXACT, LIKELY, AMBIGUOUS
   - TransferState: QUEUED, RUNNING, VERIFYING, DONE, FAILED, PAUSED
   - Fidelity: ORIGINAL, GPS_STRIPPED, TRANSCODED
2. Create MatchEntity.kt:
   @Entity(tableName = "match", primaryKeys = ["cloudItemId", "deviceItemId"], foreignKeys = [ForeignKey(CloudItemEntity, onDelete = CASCADE), ForeignKey(DeviceItemEntity, onDelete = CASCADE)])
   - cloudItemId: Long, deviceItemId: Long
   - confidence: MatchConfidence
   - evidence: String (JSON serialized evidence details)
3. Create TransferJobEntity.kt:
   @Entity(tableName = "transfer_job", foreignKeys = [ForeignKey(CloudItemEntity, onDelete = CASCADE)], indices = [Index("state"), Index("cloudItemId")])
   - id: Long (PrimaryKey, autoGenerate)
   - cloudItemId: Long
   - state: TransferState
   - destinationUri: String, bytesExpected: Long, bytesWritten: Long
   - sha256: String?, fidelity: Fidelity
   - attempts: Int, lastError: String?
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit test creating matches between cloud and device items. Verify foreign key constraints prevent orphaned matches. Test TransferJob state transitions and progress tracking.

subtasks.title: Create OriginRuleEntity and PickerRoundEntity
subtasks.description: Define the OriginRuleEntity for learned and built-in folder-to-origin mapping rules, and PickerRoundEntity for tracking picker session history.
subtasks.details:
1. Create enums in com.gankdat.pomegranate.data.db.entity:

2. Create OriginRuleEntity.kt:
   @Entity(tableName = "origin_rule", indices = [Index("pattern")])
   - id: Long (PrimaryKey, autoGenerate)
   - source: OriginSource
   - pattern: String (regex or glob pattern for filename/folder matching)
   - originLabel: String (e.g., "Camera", "Screenshots", "WhatsApp")
   - confidence: Float (0.0-1.0, higher = more certain)
3. Create PickerRoundEntity.kt:
   @Entity(tableName = "picker_round")

   - createdAt: Long (timestamp)
   - itemCount: Int (number of items selected in this round)
   - state: String (e.g., "ACTIVE", "EXPIRED", "INDEXED")
4. Ensure PickerRound links to CloudItems via sessionId foreign key relationship (CloudItem references sessionId)
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit test origin rule matching logic. Verify picker round creation and item count tracking. Test querying cloud items by session ID.

subtasks.title: Implement TypeConverters for all enum types and JSON evidence
subtasks.description: Create Room TypeConverters to handle serialization of all enum types (MediaGroupKind, MatchConfidence, TransferState, Fidelity, OriginSource) and the JSON evidence field.
subtasks.details:

   @TypeConverters annotation class
2. Add converters for each enum:
   - MediaGroupKind: @TypeConverter fun fromMediaGroupKind(kind: MediaGroupKind): String = kind.name
   - @TypeConverter fun toMediaGroupKind(value: String): MediaGroupKind = MediaGroupKind.valueOf(value)
   - MatchConfidence: same pattern
   - TransferState: same pattern
   - Fidelity: same pattern
   - OriginSource: same pattern
3. Add evidence JSON converter (simple String passthrough, or use kotlinx.serialization if complex parsing needed):
   - Evidence is stored as JSON string, no conversion needed at Room layer
   - Create sealed class Evidence in domain layer later for type-safe access
4. Register Converters at Database level via @TypeConverters annotation on the Database class

tasks.title: Build runtime permissions flow for media access
tasks.description: Implement the runtime permissions request flow for READ_MEDIA_IMAGES and READ_MEDIA_VIDEO (Android 13+) with proper rationale screens, handling of partial grants (Android 14+ visual user selected), and graceful degradation.
tasks.details:
1. Create package `com.gankdat.pomegranate.ui.permissions`.
2. Add permissions to AndroidManifest.xml:
   - READ_MEDIA_IMAGES, READ_MEDIA_VIDEO (API 33+)
   - READ_MEDIA_VISUAL_USER_SELECTED (API 34+)
   - No WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (not needed, using SAF).
3. Create `PermissionState` sealed class: Granted, PartiallyGranted (selectedPhotosAccess), Denied, PermanentlyDenied.
4. Create `PermissionViewModel` that tracks current permission state and handles requests.
5. Create `PermissionRationaleScreen` Composable:
   - Explain why the app needs media access (to scan photos/videos on device).
   - Explain what the app does NOT do (no upload, no analytics).
   - "Grant access" button triggers permission request.
6. Handle `shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale` for re-prompting.
7. Handle permanent denial: show screen with "Open Settings" button using `Intent(Settings.ACTION_APPLICATION_DETAILS_SETTINGS)`.
8. For Android 14+ partial grant (READ_MEDIA_VISUAL_USER_SELECTED), show a "Select more photos" option that re-requests.
9. Use Activity Result APIs (rememberLauncherForActivityResult) for permission requests.
10. Persist permission state awareness in DataStore to show appropriate UI on next launch.
tasks.testStrategy: Manual testing on Android 13, 14, and 15 devices/emulators: verify rationale screen shows before first request; verify handling of grant, deny, and permanent deny; verify partial grant flow on Android 14+; verify Settings deep link works.

subtasks.title: Add permission declarations to AndroidManifest.xml
subtasks.description: Declare READ_MEDIA_IMAGES, READ_MEDIA_VIDEO (API 33+), and READ_MEDIA_VISUAL_USER_SELECTED (API 34+) permissions in AndroidManifest.xml with proper maxSdkVersion constraints where applicable.
subtasks.details:
Edit app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml to add:
1. `<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.READ_MEDIA_IMAGES" />` (implicitly API 33+ only)
2. `<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.READ_MEDIA_VISUAL_USER_SELECTED" />` (API 34+)
3. `<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.READ_MEDIA_VIDEO" />`

Do NOT add WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE or READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE as the app uses SAF for writes. Ensure permissions are placed before the <application> tag. Add XML comments explaining API level requirements for future maintainers.
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify AndroidManifest.xml passes lint checks. Build the APK and use `aapt dump permissions` to confirm declared permissions. Test install on API 33 and API 34+ devices to ensure no permission-related install failures.

subtasks.title: Create PermissionState sealed class and PermissionViewModel
subtasks.description: Implement the PermissionState sealed class modeling all permission states and PermissionViewModel to track and manage permission requests using Activity Result APIs.
subtasks.details:
Create package `com.gankdat.pomegranate.ui.permissions` with:

1. `PermissionState.kt` - sealed class with:
   - `object Granted` - full media access
   - `data class PartiallyGranted(val selectedPhotosOnly: Boolean)` - Android 14+ visual user selected
   - `object Denied` - user denied but can re-ask
   - `object PermanentlyDenied` - user denied with 'Don't ask again'
   - `object NotRequested` - initial state before any request

2. `PermissionViewModel.kt` - AndroidViewModel that:
   - Exposes `permissionState: StateFlow<PermissionState>`
   - Has `checkCurrentPermissions(context: Context)` to query ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission
   - Has `updatePermissionResult(permissions: Map<String, Boolean>)` to process Activity Result callback
   - Detects partial grant by checking READ_MEDIA_VISUAL_USER_SELECTED granted while others denied
   - Uses Build.VERSION.SDK_INT checks for API-specific logic

3. Use ActivityResultContracts.RequestMultiplePermissions for the permission request.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit tests: verify PermissionState transitions for all scenarios (grant all, deny all, partial grant, permanent denial). Test ViewModel correctly interprets permission results from mock contexts. Test API version branching with mocked Build.VERSION.SDK_INT values where possible.

subtasks.title: Build PermissionRationaleScreen Composable with explanations
subtasks.description: Create the PermissionRationaleScreen Composable that explains why media access is needed, what the app does NOT do (privacy assurances), and provides a clear call-to-action button.
subtasks.details:
Create `PermissionRationaleScreen.kt` in `com.gankdat.pomegranate.ui.permissions`:

1. Material 3 Composable with:
   - Icon/illustration representing photo scanning
   - Title: "Access Your Photos & Videos"
   - Body explaining: "Pomegranate needs to scan photos and videos on this device to show you what exists locally vs only in Google Photos."
   - Privacy section with bullet points:
     • "Your media never leaves this device"
     • "No analytics or tracking"
     • "No uploads to any server"
   - Primary button: "Grant Access" that triggers permission request
   - Secondary text link: "Learn more" (optional, links to in-app help)

2. Use `rememberLauncherForActivityResult(ActivityResultContracts.RequestMultiplePermissions())` to handle the permission request.

3. Pass appropriate permissions array based on API level: `[READ_MEDIA_IMAGES, READ_MEDIA_VIDEO]` for API 33, plus `READ_MEDIA_VISUAL_USER_SELECTED` for API 34+.

4. Ensure all interactive elements have contentDescription for TalkBack accessibility.

5. Support both light and dark themes via MaterialTheme.
subtasks.testStrategy: Manual testing: verify screen renders correctly in light/dark mode. Verify TalkBack reads all content descriptions. Verify button triggers permission dialog. UI test: verify Composable snapshot matches design across configurations.

subtasks.title: Implement shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale handling
subtasks.description: Add logic to detect when shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale returns true (user previously denied) and show the rationale screen before re-requesting permissions.
subtasks.details:
Enhance PermissionViewModel and UI flow:

1. In PermissionViewModel, add `shouldShowRationale(activity: Activity): Boolean` that checks `ActivityCompat.shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale()` for both READ_MEDIA_IMAGES and READ_MEDIA_VIDEO.

2. Create decision logic in the permission flow:
   - If permissions already granted → navigate to main screen
   - If shouldShowRationale is true → show PermissionRationaleScreen
   - If first time (no denial history) → can show rationale or request directly based on UX preference
   - If shouldShowRationale is false AND previously denied → permanent denial

3. Track denial history in ViewModel state to distinguish first-time denial from permanent denial (shouldShowRationale returns false in both first request and permanent denial scenarios).

4. Update PermissionRationaleScreen to show slightly different messaging when it's a re-request ("We need this permission to..." vs "You previously denied...").

5. Ensure the flow handles configuration changes (screen rotation) without losing state.
subtasks.testStrategy: Manual testing on device: deny permission once, verify rationale screen appears on next request. Test flow after clearing app data (first-time state). Unit tests: verify ViewModel correctly interprets shouldShowRationale return values in combination with denial history.

subtasks.title: Handle Android 14+ partial grants with READ_MEDIA_VISUAL_USER_SELECTED
subtasks.description: Implement UI and logic for Android 14+ partial grant scenario where user selects specific photos via READ_MEDIA_VISUAL_USER_SELECTED, including option to select more photos.
subtasks.details:
Handle the Android 14+ visual media picker partial grant:

1. In PermissionViewModel, detect partial grant state:
   - READ_MEDIA_VISUAL_USER_SELECTED granted = true
   - READ_MEDIA_IMAGES or READ_MEDIA_VIDEO granted = false
   - This indicates user chose "Select photos" instead of "Allow all"

2. Create `PartialAccessBanner` Composable:
   - Shows in main UI when in PartiallyGranted state
   - Message: "Pomegranate can only see photos you've selected. Some device photos may be missing from the census."
   - Action button: "Select More Photos" that re-launches permission request
   - Dismiss option that persists choice via DataStore

3. When user taps "Select More Photos":
   - Re-request READ_MEDIA_IMAGES and READ_MEDIA_VIDEO
   - System shows photo picker again, user can add more photos
   - After selection, re-run device census for new items

4. Update PermissionState.PartiallyGranted to include count of selected items if available (via MediaStore query count).

5. Ensure app functions correctly in partial grant mode—device scanner should only see MediaStore items the app has access to.
subtasks.testStrategy: Manual testing on Android 14+ device: grant partial access, verify banner appears, verify "Select More" re-launches picker, verify newly selected photos appear in census. Test that app gracefully handles partial access without crashes.

subtasks.title: Implement permanent denial flow with Settings deep link and persistence
subtasks.description: Build the permanent denial handling flow that shows a screen with explanation and Settings deep link, plus persist permission state awareness in DataStore for appropriate UI on next launch.
subtasks.details:
Handle permanent denial and persistence:

1. Create `PermissionDeniedScreen.kt` Composable:
   - Explains permissions were permanently denied
   - Message: "To scan your photos and videos, you'll need to grant access in Settings."
   - Primary button: "Open Settings" using Intent(Settings.ACTION_APPLICATION_DETAILS_SETTINGS) with app package URI
   - Secondary button: "Not Now" to continue with limited functionality
   - Include deep link to specific permission settings if available on device

2. Implement Settings intent launch:
   ```kotlin
   Intent(Settings.ACTION_APPLICATION_DETAILS_SETTINGS).apply {
       data = Uri.fromParts("package", context.packageName, null)
   }
   ```

3. Add permission state persistence to DataStore (in SettingsRepository from Task 2 or new PermissionPreferences):
   - `lastKnownPermissionState: Flow<String>` (serialized PermissionState)
   - `hasRequestedPermissionsBefore: Flow<Boolean>`
   - `partialAccessBannerDismissed: Flow<Boolean>`

4. On app launch, read persisted state to:
   - Show appropriate screen immediately (avoid flicker)
   - Re-check actual permissions in case user changed them in Settings
   - If state changed from PermanentlyDenied to Granted, update and proceed

5. Handle Activity lifecycle: when returning from Settings, re-check permissions in onResume.
subtasks.testStrategy: Manual testing: permanently deny permission (deny twice), verify denied screen appears, verify Settings button opens correct app settings page. Grant permission in Settings, return to app, verify app detects change. Test persistence: kill app after permanent denial, relaunch, verify correct screen shown immediately. Test across API 33/34/35 devices.

8. Implement Keystore-backed token storage:

9. Handle token refresh (expires_in tracking).

11. Never log tokens; wipe all on revoke.

   - Load existing key from KeyStore if present.
   - Otherwise generate new AES key with KeyGenParameterSpec.Builder:
     - setKeySize(256)

     - setEncryptionPaddings(KeyProperties.ENCRYPTION_PADDING_NONE)
     - setUserAuthenticationRequired(false) (app handles auth).

   - Cipher.getInstance("AES/GCM/NoPadding").
   - cipher.init(Cipher.ENCRYPT_MODE, key) - let system generate IV.
   - Prepend cipher.iv to cipher.doFinal(plaintext.toByteArray()).
4. Implement decrypt(ciphertext: ByteArray): String:
   - Extract IV (first 12 bytes), encrypted data (rest).
   - cipher.init(Cipher.DECRYPT_MODE, key, GCMParameterSpec(128, iv)).
5. Store encrypted tokens with Base64 encoding in SharedPreferences (app-private, not backed up).
6. Implement clearTokens() to remove stored tokens and optionally delete the key.

subtasks.title: Add token refresh logic and revocation handling

subtasks.details:
1. Complete AuthRepositoryImpl.refreshToken(): AuthResult:
   - Load encrypted refresh_token from TokenStorage.
   - If no refresh_token, return NeedsReauth.
   - POST to TOKEN_ENDPOINT with grant_type=refresh_token, refresh_token=<token>, client_id.
   - On success, update stored access_token and expires_at.
   - On 400/401 error (invalid_grant), return NeedsReauth - this handles Testing mode 7-day expiry.
2. Track token expiry: store expires_at = currentTimeMillis() + (expires_in * 1000) - 60000 (1-min buffer).
3. Implement getAccessToken(): String?:
   - Check if current access_token is expired.
   - If expired, call refreshToken() automatically.
   - Return valid token or null if refresh fails.
4. Implement revokeAndClear():
   - POST to REVOKE_ENDPOINT with token=<access_token> (revokes all tokens).
   - Call TokenStorage.clearTokens() regardless of revoke success.
   - Delete Keystore key.
   - Clear any in-memory token state.
5. Implement isAuthenticated(): Flow<Boolean> that observes token presence.
6. All operations must be idempotent and safe to call multiple times.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit tests: verify refresh uses correct grant_type; verify expires_at calculation; verify getAccessToken triggers refresh when expired; verify revokeAndClear wipes all data. subtasks.title: Implement exponential backoff retry logic with attempt tracking
subtasks.description: Add exponential backoff retry mechanism to TransferWorker with maximum 5 attempts per job, attempt counter persistence, and proper error categorization for retryable vs fatal failures.
subtasks.details:
1. In TransferWorker, after a job fails, increment attempts field in TransferJobEntity.
2. Define MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5 constant.
3. Categorize failures as retryable (network timeout, server 5xx) vs fatal (404, hash mismatch, storage full).
4. For retryable failures with attempts < MAX_ATTEMPTS:
   a. Calculate backoff delay: initialDelay * 2^(attempts-1) with jitter (e.g., 30s base, max 10 min).
   b. Set job state to QUEUED (will be picked up by next worker run).
   c. Store lastError with failure reason.
5. For fatal failures OR attempts >= MAX_ATTEMPTS:
   a. Set job state to FAILED.
   b. Store detailed lastError including failure type.
6. Create RetryStrategy sealed class: Retry(delayMs), Fail, with fun categorize(exception: Exception): RetryStrategy.
7. Update TransferJobEntity to track createdAt, lastAttemptAt for retry timing.
8. Worker should skip jobs that were retried too recently (respect backoff).
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit tests: test retry on network failure with attempts < 5; test fail on attempts >= 5; test fatal errors fail immediately; test backoff delay calculation; test retryable vs fatal categorization for various exceptions. Test lastError is recorded correctly.

subtasks.title: Handle baseUrl expiry with session refresh before download
subtasks.description: Implement baseUrl expiration checking before each download attempt, triggering a Picker API session re-list if URLs have expired, and updating CloudItemEntity with fresh URLs.
subtasks.details:
1. Before downloading a cloud item, check CloudItemEntity.baseUrlExpiresAt against System.currentTimeMillis().
2. Add buffer (e.g., 5 minutes) to expiry check to avoid edge cases.
3. If expired or near-expiry:
   a. Retrieve sessionId from CloudItemEntity.
   b. Call Picker API listMediaItems for that session (Task 10 integration point).
   c. Update CloudItemEntity.baseUrl and baseUrlExpiresAt with fresh values.
   d. If session expired entirely (API returns error), mark job as FAILED with 'session_expired' error.
4. Create UrlRefresher class/interface to abstract this logic, injectable into TransferWorker.
5. Handle rate limiting on Picker API: if refresh fails due to rate limit, return Result.retry() from worker.
6. Track refresh attempts to avoid infinite refresh loops.
7. Consider batching: if multiple jobs from same session need refresh, refresh once for all.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit tests: test expired URL triggers refresh; test near-expiry triggers refresh; test valid URL proceeds without refresh; test session-expired error handling; test batch refresh for multiple jobs. Mock Picker API responses.

7. Add fun observeWorkStatus(): Flow<WorkInfo> for UI observation.

tasks.title: Implement SAF file writer with folder layout and verification
tasks.description: Build the SAF file writer that downloads media from Picker URLs, writes to the user's chosen destination with the YYYY/YYYY-MM/Origin folder layout, verifies integrity, and registers with MediaStore.
tasks.details:
1. Create `TransferDownloader` class in `com.gankdat.pomegranate.transfer`.
2. Implement file download:
   - Open HttpsURLConnection to baseUrl + "=d" (photo) or "=dv" (video).
   - Stream to temporary file in app cache.
   - Track bytes downloaded for progress.
3. Implement folder layout creation via SAF:
   - Root: user's chosen destination URI.
   - Create `Pomegranate/` if not exists.
   - Create `YYYY/` for year.
   - Create `YYYY-MM/` for month.
   - Create `<Origin>/` if inferred origin exists.
   - Use `DocumentsContract.createDocument` for folders.
   - Cache folder URIs to avoid repeated lookups.
4. Write file to final location:
   - Create document with `DocumentsContract.createDocument`.
   - Copy from temp file using ContentResolver streams.
   - Delete temp file.
5. Implement verification:
   - Verify size matches expected (from Picker metadata).
   - Compute SHA-256 of written file.
   - Store hash in TransferJobEntity.
   - Only mark DONE after verification passes.
6. Determine fidelity badge:
   - GPS_STRIPPED for all photos (Picker strips GPS).
   - TRANSCODED for all videos (Picker transcodes).
   - Store in TransferJobEntity.fidelity.
7. Register with MediaStore:
   - Use `MediaStore.Images.Media.getContentUri(EXTERNAL)` or Video.
   - Insert row with file path (convert SAF URI to file path if possible).
   - Or use `MediaScannerConnection.scanFile`.
8. Handle sibling files:
   - Download all siblings together.
   - Place in same folder.
   - Group verification.
9. Handle motion photo video halves:
   - Photo via `=d`, video via `=dv`.
   - Name video as `{basename}.mp4`.

subtasks.title: Create TransferDownloader with HttpsURLConnection streaming to temp file

subtasks.details: Create `TransferDownloader` class in `com.gankdat.pomegranate.transfer` package. Implement `downloadToTemp(baseUrl: String, mediaType: MediaType): TempDownloadResult` that: 1) Opens HttpsURLConnection to `baseUrl + "=d"` for photos or `baseUrl + "=dv"` for videos (Picker download suffixes). 2) Sets appropriate timeouts and User-Agent. 3) Creates temp file in `context.cacheDir` with unique name. 4) Streams response body to temp file using buffered streams (8KB buffer). 5) Tracks bytes downloaded and emits progress via callback or Flow. 6) Returns `TempDownloadResult(tempFile, bytesDownloaded, contentType)`. Handle connection errors, timeouts, and partial downloads. Ensure temp files are cleaned up on failure. Use `withContext(Dispatchers.IO)` for all network/file operations.

subtasks.details: Create `SafFolderManager` class that manages folder creation and caching. Implement: 1) `getOrCreateDestinationFolder(rootUri: Uri, dateTaken: LocalDate, origin: String?): Uri` that creates the full path. 2) Use `DocumentsContract.createDocument(resolver, parentUri, DocumentsContract.Document.MIME_TYPE_DIR, name)` for each level. 3) Check if folder exists first using `DocumentsContract.findDocumentPath` or query children to avoid duplicates. 4) Cache folder URIs in memory using `LruCache<String, Uri>` keyed by path string (e.g., "Pomegranate/2024/2024-03/Camera"). 5) Handle the case where Origin is null (place directly in YYYY-MM folder). 6) Format folder names correctly: "Pomegranate", year as "YYYY", month as "YYYY-MM". Implementation: 1) Create document using `DocumentsContract.createDocument(resolver, folderUri, mimeType, filename)`. 2) Open output stream via `contentResolver.openOutputStream(documentUri)`. 3) Open input stream from temp file. 4) Copy using buffered streams with progress tracking. 5) Flush and close streams properly in finally block. 6) Delete temp file after successful copy. 7) Return the final document URI. Handle filename conflicts by appending counter (e.g., "IMG_001 (1).jpg"). Verify the created document exists after write. Throw descriptive exceptions for SAF permission errors, storage full, or I/O failures. Use `use {}` blocks for auto-closing streams.

subtasks.title: Add verification with size check and SHA-256 computation
subtasks.description: Implement integrity verification that confirms file size matches expected metadata and computes SHA-256 hash for the transferred file.
subtasks.details: Create `TransferVerifier` class in transfer package. Implement: 1) `verifySize(documentUri: Uri, expectedSize: Long): Boolean` - query document size via `DocumentsContract.getDocumentColumn` or open stream and count bytes. 2) `computeSha256(documentUri: Uri): String` - read file via ContentResolver, compute hash using `MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256")`, return hex string. 3) `verify(documentUri: Uri, expectedSize: Long): VerificationResult` combining both checks. Store computed hash in TransferJobEntity.sha256Hash field. Only transition job state to DONE after verification passes. On verification failure: delete the corrupted file, mark job as FAILED with error details, allow retry. Use 8KB buffer for hash computation to balance memory and performance. All file reads must use `withContext(Dispatchers.IO)`.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit tests: verify SHA-256 computation produces correct hashes for known inputs, test size mismatch detection. Integration tests: write file with known content, verify hash matches expected, simulate corruption and verify detection.

subtasks.title: Determine and store fidelity badge for transferred files

subtasks.details: Create `FidelityClassifier` in transfer package. Define `Fidelity` enum in data package: `ORIGINAL`, `GPS_STRIPPED`, `TRANSCODED`. Implement `classifyFidelity(mediaType: MediaType, sourceType: SourceType): Fidelity`. For Google Picker source: all photos get `GPS_STRIPPED` (Picker strips EXIF GPS), all videos get `TRANSCODED` (Picker transcodes all videos). Document these limitations clearly in code comments referencing Picker API docs. Store fidelity in `TransferJobEntity.fidelity` column. Future-proof: when Takeout source is added, it can return `ORIGINAL`. UI will use this to show appropriate badge/warning. Add fidelity to the verification result so it's captured at the right time. The fidelity determination happens after successful download, before marking job complete.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit tests: verify correct fidelity assignment for photo vs video, verify enum serialization for Room. Test edge cases: motion photos (photo half GPS_STRIPPED, video half TRANSCODED).

subtasks.title: Register pulled files with MediaStore

subtasks.details: Create `MediaStoreRegistrar` class. Implement `registerWithMediaStore(documentUri: Uri, mimeType: String, dateTaken: Long?)`. Two approaches to try: 1) Primary: Use `MediaScannerConnection.scanFile(context, arrayOf(filePath), arrayOf(mimeType), callback)` - but need to convert SAF URI to file path which may not always be possible. 2) Fallback: Manually insert into `MediaStore.Images.Media` or `MediaStore.Video.Media` with content values (DISPLAY_NAME, MIME_TYPE, DATE_TAKEN, SIZE, RELATIVE_PATH if determinable). Handle both internal storage and SD card volumes. For SAF URIs that can't be converted to paths, attempt to use `MediaStore.Files.getContentUri` with the document ID. Log warning if registration fails but don't fail the transfer - the file is already safely written. Return registration success status for potential UI indication.

subtasks.description: Implement coordinated download and placement of sibling files (RAW+JPEG, live photos) and motion photo components (photo + video halves).

Implement: 1) `downloadSiblingGroup(mediaGroup: MediaGroupEntity): List<TransferResult>` that downloads all siblings together. 2) Place all siblings in the same destination folder. 3) For motion photos: download photo via `=d` suffix, download video via `=dv` suffix, name video as `{photoBasename}.mp4` (e.g., PXL_20240101.jpg becomes PXL_20240101.mp4). 4) Verify all siblings as a group - if one fails, mark entire group for retry. 5) Update all sibling TransferJobEntity records together atomically. 6) Handle the case where only some siblings are cloud-only (only download what's needed). Link sibling jobs via `TransferJobEntity.groupId` field. Ensure folder creation happens once for the group. Register all siblings with MediaStore. The UI should show grouped progress for sibling transfers.

subtasks.description: Create the network security configuration XML file in res/xml/ that explicitly disables cleartext traffic and configures TLS requirements for all network communications.
subtasks.details:
Create res/xml/network_security_config.xml with the following configuration:
1. Set cleartextTrafficPermitted="false" at base-config level (explicit for safety, even though it's default for minSdk 30).
2. Configure to trust only system CAs - do NOT add custom trust anchors or certificate pins.
3. Use <base-config> rather than domain-specific configs since all traffic goes to Google APIs.
4. Avoid certificate pinning for Google domains as their certs rotate frequently and this would cause breakage.

Example structure:
```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<network-security-config>
    <base-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="false">
        <trust-anchors>
            <certificates src="system" />
        </trust-anchors>
    </base-config>
</network-security-config>
```

This ensures all network traffic uses HTTPS with system-trusted certificates only.
